paragraphs.sourceText: Listen to the following passage. Altogether the passage will be read to you four times. During the first reading, which will be done at normal speed, listen and try to understand the meaning. For the second and third readings, the passage, except the first sentence, will be read sentence by sentence, or phrase by phrase, with intervals of 15 seconds. The last reading will be done at normal speed again and during this time you should check your work. You will then be given ONE minute to check your work once more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 听下面这段话。这篇文章总共会读给你四遍。在第一次阅读时，将以正常速度完成，聆听并尝试理解其含义。第二、三读时，除第一句外，逐句或逐词朗读，间隔15秒。最后一次阅读将再次以正常速度完成，在此期间您应该检查您的工作。然后您将有一分钟的时间再次检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Decide which of the words given in the box below would best complete the passage if inserted in the corresponding blank. The words can be used ONCE ONLY. Mark the letter for each word on ANSWER SHEET TWO.

Traditionally, the subject of metaphor tends to come up in literature classes where everyone learns that a metaphor is a figure of speech: “No man is an island.” It’s learned first as an element of (31) ________, a way to polish language. Metaphors are first brought to our attention in poems, mostly, but we’re taught to recognize them in stories and songs too: “She’s got the moon in her eyes.” Consequently, many people associate metaphors most (32) ________ with the literary arts and understand them as a matter of language — a figure of speech. But metaphors are also a tool for discovering and connecting ideas — a figure of thought.

Whether (33) ________ or conceptual, metaphors are acts of imagination. To see one thing in terms of another is to think (34) ________. That is, we set up correspondences between two concepts. This involves partially structuring our understanding of an abstract object (love, for example) by seeing it in terms of a rather (35) ________ object (say, a garden). Thus we can think and talk about “cultivating” (36) “________” and “tending to” our friendships. The process of setting up such correspondences is called “mapping.” By mapping gardens onto love, which are otherwise two (37) ________ conceptual domains, we invite a comparison and give visible forms to an abstract idea. “Gardens” is the source domain from which we draw properties that can be (38) ________ to “love,” the target domain. Through metaphors, both conventional and unconventional, we build and lay claim to (39) ________ among otherwise discrete phenomena. The habit of metaphorical thinking belongs to everyone. Metaphor is very much involved in the way they (40) ________, talk about, and most of all, experience the world.

In this section there are three passages followed by ten multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十个多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Six months before she died, my grandmother moved into an old people’s home and I visited her there. She was sitting in the living room with about fifteen other residents, mostly women, half of them asleep. The room was clean and warm, with flowers and pictures, and the care assistants were kind and cheerful. A talk show was on the television, and the only other sound was snoring and embarrassing digestive noises. People only moved when they needed to be helped to the bathroom. It was depressing. Gran talked a lot about how much she missed seeing her grandchildren, but I knew from my sister that they hated going to visit her there and, to be perfectly honest, I couldn’t wait to get away myself.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 我祖母去世前六个月，搬进了一家敬老院，我去那里看望了她。她和大约十五名其他居民坐在客厅里，其中大部分是女性，其中一半人正在睡觉。房间干净温馨，有鲜花和图画，护理人员友善开朗。电视上正在播放脱口秀节目，唯一的声音就是鼾声和令人尴尬的消化噪音。人们只有在需要帮助去洗手间时才会移动。真是令人沮丧。奶奶说了很多她多么想念见到孙子们​​，但我从姐姐那里知道，他们讨厌去那里看望她，说实话，我迫不及待地想亲自离开。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) So I was interested to read a newspaper article about a new concept in old people’s homes. The idea is simple, but revolutionary: combining a residential home for the elderly with a nursery school in the same building. The children and the residents eat lunch together and share activities such as music, painting, gardening and caring for the pets which the residents are encouraged to keep. In the afternoons, the residents enjoy reading or telling stories to the children and, if a child is feeling sad or tired, there is always a kind lap to sit on and a cuddle. There are trips out and birthday parties too.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 所以我有兴趣阅读一篇关于老人之家新概念的报纸文章。这个想法很简单，但却是革命性的：将敬老院和幼儿园合并在同一栋大楼内。孩子们和居民一起吃午餐，并分享音乐、绘画、园艺和照顾鼓励居民饲养的宠物等活动。下午，居民们喜欢给孩子们读书或讲故事，如果孩子感到悲伤或疲倦，总有一个友善的腿可以让他们坐下来并拥抱他们。也有外出旅行和生日聚会。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) The advantages are enormous for everyone concerned. The children are happy because they get a lot more individual attention and respond well because someone has time for them. They also learn that old people are not different or frightening in any way. And of course, they see illness and death and learn to accept them. The residents are happy because they feel useful and needed. They are more active and more interested in life when the children are around and they take more interest in their appearance too. And the staff are happy because they see an improvement in the physical and psychological health of the residents.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 对于所有相关方来说，其优势都是巨大的。孩子们很高兴，因为他们得到了更多的个人关注，并且因为有人有时间陪伴他们而反应良好。他们还了解到，老年人在任何方面都没有什么不同或令人恐惧。当然，他们看到疾病和死亡并学会接受它们。居民们很高兴，因为他们觉得自己有用、被需要。当孩子们在身边时，他们会更加活跃，对生活更加感兴趣，对自己的外表也更加感兴趣。工作人员很高兴，因为他们看到居民的身心健康得到改善。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) Nowadays there is less and less contact between the old and the young. There are many reasons for this, including the breakdown of the extended family, working parents with no time to care for ageing relations, families that have moved away and smaller flats with no room for grandparents. But the result is the same: increasing numbers of children without grandparents and old people who have no contact with children. And more old people who are lonely and feel useless, along with more and more families with young children who desperately need more support. It’s a major problem in many societies.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4)现在老年人和年轻人的接触越来越少。造成这种情况的原因有很多，包括大家庭的破裂、工作父母没有时间照顾年迈的亲戚、搬走的家庭以及没有空间容纳祖父母的较小的公寓。但结果是一样的：没有祖父母的孩子和与孩子没有接触的老人的数量不断增加。越来越多的老人感到孤独和无用，越来越多的家庭有年幼的孩子，迫切需要更多的支持。这是许多社会的一个主要问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) That’s why inter-generational programs, designed to bring the old and the young together, are growing in popularity all over the world, supported by UNESCO and other local and international organizations. There are examples of successful initiatives all over the world. Using young people to teach IT skills to older people is one obvious example. Using old people as volunteer assistants in schools is another, perhaps reading with children who need extra attention. There are schemes which involve older people visiting families who are having problems, maybe looking after the children for a while to give the tired mother a break. Or “adopt a grandparent” schemes in which children write letters or visit a lonely old person in their area. There are even holiday companies that specialize in holidays for children and grandparents together. One of the successful schemes pairs young volunteers with old people who are losing their sight. The young people help with practical things such as helping with online shopping, and the older people can pass on their knowledge and experience to their young visitors. For example, a retired judge may be paired with a teenager who wants to study law. Lasting friendships often develop.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 这就是为什么在联合国教科文组织和其他当地和国际组织的支持下，旨在将老年人和年轻人聚集在一起的代际计划在世界各地越来越受欢迎。世界各地都有成功举措的例子。利用年轻人向老年人传授 IT 技能就是一个明显的例子。另一种方法是让老年人在学校担任志愿者助理，也许可以和需要额外照顾的孩子一起读书。有一些计划让老年人拜访有问题的家庭，也许可以照顾孩子一段时间，让疲惫的母亲休息一下。或者“收养祖父母”计划，其中孩子们写信或拜访他们所在地区的孤独老人。甚至还有专门为孩子和祖父母一起度假的度假公司。其中一项成功的计划将年轻志愿者与失明的老年人配对。年轻人可以帮助做一些实际的事情，比如帮助网上购物，而老年人可以将他们的知识和经验传授给年轻的游客。例如，一位退休法官可能会与一位想要学习法律的青少年配对。持久的友谊往往会发展。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) But it isn’t only the individuals concerned who gain from inter-generational activities. The advantages to society are enormous too. If older people can understand and accept the youth of today, and vice versa, there will be less conflict in a community. In a world where the number of old people is increasing, we need as much understanding and tolerance as possible. Modern society has isolated people into age groups and now we need to rediscover what “community” really means. And we can use the strengths of one generation to help another. Then perhaps getting old won’t be such a depressing prospect after all.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 但从代际活动中获益的不仅仅是相关个人。对社会的好处也是巨大的。如果老年人能够理解并接受当今的年轻人，反之亦然，社区中的冲突就会减少。在老年人口不断增加的世界里，我们需要尽可能多的理解和宽容。现代社会将人们划分为不同的年龄段，现在我们需要重新发现“社区”的真正含义。我们可以利用一代人的优势来帮助另一代人。那么也许变老就不再是一个令人沮丧的前景了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The following are the advantages of inter-generational activities EXCEPT ________.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 以下是代际活动的优点，除了________。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) My father’s youngest brother, Uncle Chul, shared the Lee’s famously bad reaction to liquor, which was to turn beet-red in the face, grow dizzy and finally get sick. In spite of this, he was always happy to stay up late at family gatherings. After a few glasses of whisky he would really loosen up, and, with the notable exception of my mother, we all appreciated his rough language and stories. Only when Mother came in from the kitchen would his talk soften, for he knew he had always fallen short in her eyes. If they were ever alone together, say in the kitchen, after dinner, he would use the most decorous (得体的) voice in asking for a glass or a fresh bucket of ice, and even offer to help load the dishwasher or run an errand to the store.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 我父亲最小的弟弟，哲叔叔，和李家一样对酒精有众所周知的不良反应，就是脸色变红，头晕，最后生病了。尽管如此，他总是乐于在家庭聚会上熬夜。喝了几杯威士忌后，他真的会放松下来，而且，除了我母亲之外，我们都欣赏他粗俗的语言和故事。只有当母亲从厨房进来时，他的语气才变得柔和，因为他知道自己在她眼里一直是不够的。如果他们单独在一起，比如在厨房里，晚饭后，他会用最得体的声音要一杯或一桶新鲜的冰块，甚至主动帮忙装洗碗机或去商店跑腿。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) On one of those nights we sped off, both happy for a break in the long evening. He asked me about school, what sports I was playing, but the conversation inevitably turned toward my parents, and particularly my mother — how much she had invested in me, that I was her great hope. I thought it was odd that he was speaking this way, like my other relatives, and I answered with some criticism of her — that she was too anxious and overbearing. He stared at me and, with a hard solemnity I had not heard from him before, said that my mother was one of the finest people one could ever know. He kept a grip on the wheel and in the ensuing quiet of the drive I could sense how he must have both admired and despised her. In many respects, my mother was an unrelenting woman. She tended to measure people by the mark of a few principles of conduct: ask no help from anyone, always plan for the long run and practice (her own variation of) the golden rule, which was to treat others much better than oneself.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 在其中一个夜晚，我们加速出发，两人都很高兴能在漫长的夜晚得到休息。他问我学校的情况，参加什么运动，但话题不可避免地转向了我的父母，尤其是我的母亲——她在我身上投入了多少，我是她最大的希望。我觉得他这样说话很奇怪，就像我的其他亲戚一样，我对她进行了一些批评——她太焦虑、太专横了。他盯着我，用一种我以前从未听过的严肃态度说，我的母亲是人们所认识的最优秀的人之一。他紧紧握住方向盘，在随后的安静的行驶中，我能感觉到他一定既钦佩又鄙视她。从很多方面来说，我的母亲都是一个不屈不挠的女人。她倾向于用一些行为原则来衡量一个人：不向任何人寻求帮助，总是为长远规划并实践（她自己的）黄金法则，即对待别人比自己好得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) In her mind, Uncle Chul sorely lacked on all these accounts. In the weeks following our drive, my father would be deciding whether to lend him $10,000 to start a business. As always after dinner, my parents sat in the kitchen and spoke in Korean, under the light of a fluorescent ring. My mother, in many ways the director of the family, questioned my uncle’s character and will. Hadn’t he performed poorly in school, failed to finish college? Hadn’t he spent most of his youth perfecting his skills as a black belt in tae kwon do (跆拳道) and his billiards game? Wasn’t he a gambler in spirit?
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 在她看来，楚尔叔叔非常缺乏所有这些账户。在我们开车后的几周内，我父亲会决定是否借给他 10,000 美元来创业。晚饭后，我的父母一如既往地坐在厨房里，在荧光环的灯光下用韩语说话。我的母亲在很多方面都是家庭的主导者，她质疑我叔叔的性格和意志。他不是在学校表现很差，没能读完大学吗？他年轻时的大部分时间不是都在练习跆拳道黑带和台球吗？他不就是一个精神上的赌徒吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) My father could defend him only weakly. Uncle Chul had a history of working hard only when reward was well within sight, like cash piled high on the end of a pool table. His older brothers were all respected professionals and academics. My father was a doctor, a psychiatrist who had taught himself English in order to practice in Vancouver. Uncle Chul had left Korea after a series of failed ventures and odd jobs, and found himself broke with a wife and new baby. How valuable were his tae kwon do trophies now? What could he possibly do in this country?
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 我父亲只能软弱地保护他。楚尔叔叔一向只有在回报唾手可得时才会努力工作，就像台球桌一端堆满现金一样。他的哥哥都是受人尊敬的专业人士和学者。我的父亲是一名医生、精神科医生，为了在温哥华行医，他自学了英语。在经历了一系列失败的冒险和打零工之后，哲叔叔离开了韩国，并发现自己与妻子和新生儿破产了。现在他的跆拳道奖杯有多值钱？他在这个国家能做什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) My parents argued fiercely and my father left the kitchen. But as was my mother’s way, she kept on pushing her side of the issue, thinking aloud. My father was throwing away his hard-earned money on the naive wish that his little brother had magically changed. Uncle Chul was a poor risk and even now was complaining about his present job, hauling and cleaning produce for a greengrocer. He would get to the store at 4 a.m. to prepare vegetables for the day’s selling. While he shared a sofa bed with his nephew in his older brother’s tiny apartment, his wife and infant daughter were still in Seoul, waiting for him to make enough money to send for them.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 父母吵得很激烈，父亲离开了厨房。但正如我母亲的方式一样，她继续坚持自己的立场，大声思考。我的父亲把他辛苦赚来的钱都扔掉了，天真地希望他的弟弟能够神奇地改变。楚尔叔叔的风险很小，甚至现在还在抱怨他目前的工作，为一家蔬菜水果店搬运和清洁​​农产品。他会在凌晨 4 点到达商店，准备当天销售的蔬菜。当他和侄子在哥哥的小公寓里共用一张沙发床时，他的妻子和年幼的女儿仍在首尔，等着他赚到足够的钱去接她们。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Deep in the jungles of Colombia there is a kind of flower that attracts bees with its unique perfume. In Venezuela there is a flower people collect for its large white or yellow petals. Few people ever find it, though, since it only blooms for a few days. There is a small pink and yellow flower that only grows in a very specific part of the state of Florida. It also only grows on trees, and wind or birds may spread its seeds. These flowers are some of the most rare and delicate species in all of nature. They are all types of orchids (兰花).
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 哥伦比亚丛林深处有一种花，以其独特的香味吸引蜜蜂。在委内瑞拉，人们收集一种花，因为它有白色或黄色的大花瓣。然而很少有人发现它，因为它只开花几天。有一种粉红色和黄色的小花，只生长在佛罗里达州的一个非常特定的地区。它也只生长在树上，风或鸟可以传播它的种子。这些花是自然界中最稀有、最精致的物种。它们都是兰花的种类。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) For hundreds of years orchids have been prized discoveries of collectors and adventurers hoping to find new and exotic breeds of the flower. In her book The Orchid Thief, author Susan Orlean tells how in the 1800s orchids became popular in Europe, which made them very valuable. Many “orchid hunters” set out to find and bring back new types of orchids to sell. However, many of the men who went looking for the mysterious orchids met with tragedy instead.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 数百年来，兰花一直是收藏家和冒险家的珍贵发现，他们希望找到新的、奇异的花卉品种。作者苏珊·奥尔良 (Susan Orlean) 在她的《兰花小偷》一书中讲述了兰花如何在 1800 年代在欧洲流行起来，从而变得非常有价值。许多“兰花猎人”开始寻找并带回新品种的兰花进行销售。然而，许多寻找神秘兰花的人却遭遇了悲剧。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) While the plants have long been valued for their beauty, they may be even more important to science and our understanding of co-evolution. Unlike plants that can self-pollinate (自传花粉), orchids need very specific insects or birds to spread their pollen (花粉). The process by which insects, the wind, or birds spread the pollen of different flowers is called pollination. Pollen is a powder produced by plants that contains their genetic material. In order for the plants to reproduce, the pollen must be physically moved to the flower’s stigma (柱头), which contains an egg. Now the fertilized egg can become a seed. Birds and insects can pollinate plants by touching many different flowers and spreading the pollen around.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 虽然植物长期以来因其美丽而受到重视，但它们对于科学和我们对共同进化的理解可能更为重要。与自花授粉的植物不同，兰花需要非常特定的昆虫或鸟类来传播花粉。昆虫、风或鸟类传播不同花朵的花粉的过程称为授粉。花粉是植物产生的粉末，含有其遗传物质。为了使植物繁殖，花粉必须被物理地转移到含有卵的花的柱头上。现在受精卵可以成为种子。鸟类和昆虫可以通过接触许多不同的花朵并将花粉传播到周围来为植物授粉。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) Orchids evolved to attract insects and birds. Because there are many different species of orchid, there are also many different ways the orchids attract their pollinators. Orlean explains that “many species look so much like their favorite insects that the insect mistakes them for kin [other insects], and when it lands on the flower to visit, pollen sticks to its body... Another orchid imitates the shape of something that a pollinating insect likes to kill... Other species look like the mate of their pollinator, so the insect tries to mate with one orchid and then another... and spreads pollen from flower to flower each hopeless time.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (4)兰花的进化是为了吸引昆虫和鸟类。由于兰花有许多不同的品种，因此兰花吸引传粉者的方式也有许多不同。奥尔良解释说，“许多物种看起来非常像它们最喜欢的昆虫，以至于昆虫误认为它们是亲戚（其他昆虫），当它落在花朵上拜访时，花粉会粘在它的身上……另一种兰花模仿授粉昆虫喜欢杀死的东西的形状……其他物种看起来像它们传粉者的配偶，所以昆虫试图与一朵兰花交配，然后又与另一朵兰花交配……并在每次无望的情况下将花粉从一朵花传播到另一朵花。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) Other orchids don’t use their shape at all, but rather produce specialized scents to attract specific insects, such as bees, beetles or flies. Some orchids smell like cake, some like chocolate, and some like rotting meat. All these smells may seem weird, but they exist to lure creatures to their pollen and help the orchids survive. The strategies to attract insects and spread their flowers’ pollen go on and on. Each family of orchids has a unique kind of insect or bird that visits their flowers, as well as its own way of attracting them. It has worked, too. According to NOVA, a science television series, “orchid species number more than 25,000 worldwide.” That is more kinds of species than any other flower on the planet, and new ones are still being found.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 其他兰花根本不利用它们的形状，而是产生特殊的气味来吸引特定的昆虫，例如蜜蜂、甲虫或苍蝇。有的兰花闻起来像蛋糕，有的像巧克力，有的像腐肉。所有这些气味可能看起来很奇怪，但它们的存在是为了引诱生物接触它们的花粉并帮助兰花生存。吸引昆虫和传播花朵花粉的策略一直在继续。每个兰花科都有一种独特的昆虫或鸟类来拜访它们的花朵，以及吸引它们的方式。它也发挥了作用。据科普电视连续剧《NOVA》报道，“全世界兰花品种超过 25,000 种。”这比地球上任何其他花的种类都多，并且仍在不断发现新的种类。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) Orchids and the insects that pollinate them are one of the most amazing examples of evolution. Though their degree of co-dependence varies, as it is apparent that at least some orchids are more reliant on their pollinators than the pollinators are on the orchids, the degree of evolutionary specialization is still very impressive. Research suggests that certain species of orchid evolved specifically to attract orchid bees, which collect a wide variety of scents from various plants in preparation for mating. In another case, an orchid mimics a female’s smell and appearance — and the male pollinator gets nothing out of the bargain whatsoever. By tricking the insects that collect its pollen, the orchid has survived since the time of the dinosaurs.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 兰花和为其授粉的昆虫是进化最令人惊奇的例子之一。尽管它们的相互依赖程度各不相同，但显然至少有一些兰花对传粉媒介的依赖程度超过传粉媒介对兰花的依赖程度，但进化的专业化程度仍然非常令人印象深刻。研究表明，某些兰花品种是专门为了吸引兰花蜜蜂而进化的，兰花蜜蜂会从各种植物中收集各种气味，为交配做准备。在另一个例子中，兰花模仿雌性兰花的气味和外观，而雄性传粉者却没有从这笔交易中得到任何好处。通过欺骗收集花粉的昆虫，兰花从恐龙时代就得以生存。

paragraphs.sourceText: As far as technology is concerned, the world has changed for our generation, and as parents, teachers, leaders and educators, we are seeing the impact of that change on our children.
paragraphs.translationZh: 就技术而言，我们这一代的世界已经发生了变化，作为父母、教师、领导者和教育工作者，我们正在看到这种变化对我们孩子的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: The average 14-year-old now absorbs five hours’ worth of content for every hour that they are receiving information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，14 岁的孩子平均每接收一小时的信息就会吸收五个小时的内容。

paragraphs.sourceText: How? Well, your kid comes home from school and puts his headphones on. There’s a TV on in the corner, and he is checking his emails, watching vlogs, and researching his homework. Within an hour he has absorbed more information than we have in a whole afternoon.
paragraphs.translationZh: 怎么办？好吧，你的孩子放学回家，戴上耳机。角落里开着一台电视，他正在检查电子邮件、观看视频博客、研究作业。一个小时内他吸收的信息比我们整个下午吸收的信息还要多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Your kid is not “multi-tasking” as you might like to think; he does not take in separate pieces of information at exactly the same time — he is jumping between different tasks at incredible speeds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你的孩子并不像你想象的那样“同时处理多项任务”。他不会在同一时间接收不同的信息——他以令人难以置信的速度在不同的任务之间跳跃。

paragraphs.sourceText: Our generation learned at school that we usually start something, follow it through and then move on to the next thing. But the children of today no longer learn in this way; they have a fragmented attention span due to the fragmented style of learning in which they receive information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们这一代人在学校学到，我们通常会开始做某件事，坚持到底，然后继续做下一件事情。但今天的孩子们不再以这种方式学习；由于他们接收信息的学习方式分散，他们的注意力也分散。

paragraphs.sourceText: I recently gave a speech, and my point is this: Stop blaming technology and embrace it. There is no point saying “Don’t look at the computer”; instead be creative and show your child more interesting things to look at on the computer!
paragraphs.translationZh: 我最近做了一次演讲，我的观点是：停止指责技术并拥抱它。说“不要看电脑”是没有意义的；相反，要有创意，向您的孩子展示更多有趣的东西在电脑上看！

paragraphs.sourceText: Thousands of years ago people got their messages across to others by carving them on a tree or on a stone; now we have Social Media. Let’s move forward together with our children, and maybe we will all learn something along the way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 几千年前，人们通过将信息刻在树上或石头上来向他人传达信息。现在我们有了社交媒体。让我们和孩子一起前进，也许我们都会在路上学到一些东西。

Traditionally, the subject of metaphor tends to come up in literature classes where everyone learns that a metaphor is a figure of speech: “No man is an island.” It’s learned first as an element of style, a way to (31) ________ language. But metaphors are also a tool for discovering and connecting ideas — a figure of thought.
